<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command sources the PKGBUILD to extract metadata such as package names, versions, dependencies, and sources. During this phase, only the global/top-level scope of the PKGBUILD is evaluated; functions like `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package_*` are **not executed**.

In this PKGBUILD, the top-level content consists of standard variable assignments (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `arch`, `source`, `sha256sums`, etc.) and one use of command substitution: `$_source="atvv-linux-$pkgver"`. This is a simple string concatenation with no external command execution or network activity. There are no function calls, loops, or external invocations at the global scope.

All `source` and `sha256sums` entries are explicitly defined and point to the expected GitHub release. No remote code execution, data exfiltration, or suspicious operations occur during sourcing. Therefore, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD is safe.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>

No dangerous top-level code; safe to source.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
